Scripted CAD

Python Parametric Modeling · CadQuery · build123d · Pipe Vise Assembly
Three pipe-vise components modeled parametrically in Python — each part scripted twice, once with CadQuery and once with build123d, for a direct framework comparison.

Project Overview

Parametric 3D modeling in code — no GUI, no mouse, just Python and geometry.

This project models a mechanical pipe vise in Python using two open-source CAD scripting frameworks: CadQuery and build123d. The same three parts — moving jaw, spindle, and connecting wage — are implemented in each framework, producing six total scripts. The goal is to understand both APIs, their modeling primitives, and their trade-offs for parametric design work.

What I Built

  • Moving jaw body with dovetail slot, jaw face, and bolt hole pattern
  • Threaded spindle with Acme thread profile (via bd_warehouse / cq_warehouse)
  • Connecting wage (the link between spindle and jaw) with press-fit pin geometry
  • All three parts implemented in both CadQuery and build123d
  • STEP export from each script for import into FreeCAD and CastVR
  • Exploratory comparison of CadQuery's fluent chain API vs. build123d's algebraic mode

CadQuery vs. build123d

CadQuery uses a workplane-based fluent API: every operation chains off a Workplane object. build123d uses algebraic operators — + for union, - for cut, Location() * for positioning — which reads more like math than a method chain. Both wrap the same OpenCASCADE geometry kernel underneath.

Why Scripted CAD?

Traditional CAD tools record geometry as clicks. Scripted CAD records it as code — every dimension is a named variable, every feature is a reproducible function. This makes the model version-controllable, diff-able, and automatable in ways a parametric GUI model never quite achieves.

For engineering visualization work, scripted parts are also cleanly exportable to STEP without the manual cleanup a scanned or manually-drawn mesh requires.

Code Sample — build123d Spindle

from build123d import * from bd_warehouse.thread import AcmeThread # Spindle shaft shaft = Cylinder( radius=SHAFT_R, height=SHAFT_LEN ) # Acme thread section thread = AcmeThread( size="3/4-6", length=THREAD_LEN, external=True ) thread = Location((0, 0, THREAD_Z)) * thread spindle = shaft + thread
